spec_used: specs/ocr/biology-a-gateway-J247.md (+ specs/ocr/biology-a-gateway-J247-bold.md for every tier ruling)

findings.claim: The homeostasis lesson opens with no note on which paper examines it.
findings.truth: Topic B3 is assessed on Paper 1 (F1 / H3). A one-sentence scope note now says so at the top of the article.
findings.evidence: spec assessment overview: 'Paper 1 assesses content from Topics B1-B3 and B7'; 'Paper 2 assesses content from Topics B4-B6 and B7'

findings.claim: 'Blood glucose concentration is monitored continuously by the pancreas (B3.3b-c).'
findings.truth: B3.3b is the function of the skin in temperature control. Insulin control of blood sugar is B3.3c alone.
findings.evidence: bold spec B3.3b / B3.3c

findings.claim: Glucagon paragraph cited as '(B3.3b, Higher Tier)'.
findings.truth: Glucagon interacting with insulin is B3.3d, which is bold in the spec, so Higher tier only. The higher-only wrapper around it is correct and was kept.
findings.evidence: bold spec **B3.3d** 'explain how glucagon interacts with insulin to control blood sugar levels in the body'

findings.claim: Both type 1 and type 2 diabetes paragraphs cited as '(B3.3d)'.
findings.truth: Comparing type 1 and type 2 diabetes is B3.3e, a both-tier statement. B3.3d is the Higher-only glucagon statement, so the old code also implied diabetes was Higher tier.
findings.evidence: bold spec B3.3e (not bold) 'compare type 1 and type 2 diabetes and explain how they can be treated'

findings.claim: 'maintained at approximately 37 degC by the thermoregulatory centre in the brain (B3.3c)'.
findings.truth: Body temperature control is B3.3b. B3.3c is insulin. The 37 degC value itself is right.
findings.evidence: bold spec B3.3b 'describe the function of the skin in the control of body temperature'

findings.claim: MCQ 1 'Which cells in the pancreas release insulin?' offered both 'Beta cells' (keyed correct) and 'Islet cells'.
findings.truth: Beta cells ARE islet cells (islets of Langerhans), so a student who learned 'the islets produce insulin' had a second defensible answer. Distractor changed to 'Liver cells'.
findings.evidence: settled fact: islets of Langerhans contain alpha, beta and delta cells

findings.claim: Q1 typed '1 mark - Multiple Choice' but carries no options, and the mark scheme begins 'A:'.
findings.truth: It is a short recall question. Retyped '1 mark - State/Name' and the 'A:' stem removed.
findings.evidence: the question text contains no A)/B)/C)/D) options, unlike every other Multiple Choice item in this unit

findings.claim: Practice Q1, knowledge check 3 and flashcard 3 all require glucagon, with no tier flag, in a lesson tiered 'both'.
findings.truth: Glucagon appears only in B3.3d, which is bold. '(Higher tier)' prefixed on the question and the knowledge check, and appended to the flashcard question.
findings.evidence: bold spec **B3.3d**

findings.claim: The kidney lesson opens with no note on which paper examines it.
findings.truth: Topic B3 is assessed on Paper 1 (F1 / H3). Scope note added.
findings.evidence: spec assessment overview

findings.claim: Kidney excretion and osmoregulation, and selective reabsorption, both cited as '(B3.3e)'.
findings.truth: B3.3e is the diabetes comparison. Kidney water balance is B3.3g and the kidney/tubule structure is B3.3h.
findings.evidence: bold spec B3.3g, B3.3h

findings.claim: 'The amount of water reabsorbed ... is regulated by ADH (B3.3f) ... It acts on the collecting ducts and distal tubule ... making them more permeable to water' sat OUTSIDE the higher-only wrapper, unflagged.
findings.truth: B3.3f is the effect of osmotic change on cells. The ADH permeability statement is B3.3i, which is bold, so Higher tier only. The paragraph was rewritten so the both-tier statement B3.3g (kidneys vary the amount and concentration of urine) leads and the ADH mechanism is flagged 'Higher tier only'. Practice Q3, knowledge check 2, flashcards 6 and 7 and the conclusion takeaway now carry a (Higher tier) tag.
findings.evidence: bold spec **B3.3i** 'describe the effect of ADH on the permeability of the kidney tubules'; B3.3g not bold

findings.claim: 'Two main treatments exist for kidney failure (B3.3g): dialysis and kidney transplantation.'
findings.truth: B3.3g is the kidney water-balance statement. Dialysis and kidney transplants appear nowhere in this spec; the only transplant reference is 'tissue transplantation and rejection' under the stem-cell statement B6.3v. The code was removed and one sentence added saying the board has no statement on treating kidney failure.
findings.evidence: grep of the spec for 'dialysis' returns nothing; 'transplant' returns only B6.3v

findings.claim: Six B4.1 codes are wrong: levels of organisation (B4.1d), interdependence (B4.1f), abiotic/biotic factors (B4.1e), indicator species (B4.1e), trophic levels (B4.1a-b), adaptations (B4.1d).
findings.truth: Correct codes: B4.1e, B4.1g, B4.1f, B6.1b, B4.1h. Adaptations appear only in the B4.1 summary, not in any lettered statement, so the reference was reduced to B4.1.
findings.evidence: bold spec B4.1a-j; B6.1b (lichen distribution against pollution sits in its practical suggestions)

findings.claim: The energy-transfer efficiency paragraph (the 10% rule and the 10000/1000/100/10 kJ worked chain) was wrapped in higher-only and labelled '(B4.1c, Higher Tier)'; the exam tip repeats 'Higher Tier calculations of energy transfer percentage'.
findings.truth: B4.1i and B4.1j are NOT bold, so pyramids of biomass and calculating the efficiency of biomass transfers are both-tier content. The wrapper hid required Foundation material. Wrapper removed, code corrected to B4.1i-j, exam tip de-tiered. (B4.1c is the carbon and water cycles.) The arithmetic in the paragraph is correct.
findings.evidence: bold spec B4.1i, B4.1j both plain; recomputation 10000 -> 1000 -> 100 -> 10 kJ at 10% each

findings.claim: Meiosis cited '(B5.1b)'; DNA structure and 23 pairs cited '(B5.1c)'.
findings.truth: Meiotic cell division is B5.1h; B5.1b is the genome statement. DNA as a polymer, the double helix and nucleotides are B1.2a-c; B5.1c is the genome-environment-phenotype statement.
findings.evidence: bold spec B5.1b, B5.1c, B5.1h; B1.2a-c

findings.claim: The whole Protein Synthesis section (transcription, template strand, mRNA, codons, tRNA, ribosomes) is taught with no tier flag, labelled '(B5.1c, Separate-only depth)'.
findings.truth: Protein synthesis is B1.2d and B1.2e, and BOTH are bold, so they are Higher tier only. They are also not separate-only. The section is now wrapped in higher-only, the code corrected to B1.2d-e (Higher tier), and practice Q3, Q4 and Q6, knowledge checks 2 and 4, and flashcards 7, 8, 9 and 12 carry a (Higher tier) tag.
findings.evidence: bold spec **B1.2d** 'recall a simple description of protein synthesis' and **B1.2e** 'explain simply how the structure of DNA affects the proteins made in protein synthesis'

findings.claim: Fill question 4 'the _____ strand of DNA is used as a template' offered 'template' (keyed correct) and 'antisense'.
findings.truth: The antisense strand is the template strand, so the item had two correct answers. Distractor changed to 'ribosomal'.
findings.evidence: settled fact: sense strand = coding strand; antisense strand = template strand

findings.claim: 'This type of fieldwork is a key skill in biology practical work (PAG B2).'
findings.truth: PAG 2 is Testing for biological molecules. Sampling to investigate distribution and abundance is PAG 3.
findings.evidence: spec PAG table: '3 Sampling techniques - Application of appropriate sampling techniques to investigate the distribution and abundance of organisms in an ecosystem'

findings.claim: The eutrophication sequence 'is a common extended-response question'.
findings.truth: Eutrophication, algal blooms, fertiliser run-off and nitrate are not named anywhere in this spec, so the exam claim is wrong. The content is still a fair example of a negative human interaction with an ecosystem (B6.1b), and the sentence now says that instead.
findings.evidence: grep of the spec for 'eutrophic', 'algal', 'nitrate' returns nothing; 'fertilisers and pesticides' appears only in B6.2b

findings.claim: The whole Genetic Modification block - the definition of GM, the GM crop examples (golden rice, pest and herbicide resistance) and the list of concerns - is wrapped in higher-only.
findings.truth: B6.2d (genetic engineering as a process), B6.2f (benefits and risks of gene technology in agriculture) and B6.2g (biotechnological solutions) are all plain, so this is both-tier content that Foundation students were losing. Only B6.2e, the mechanism, is bold. Wrapper removed.
findings.evidence: bold spec B6.2d, B6.2f, B6.2g plain; **B6.2e** bold

findings.claim: 'inserting it into the target organism's DNA using a vector (often a bacterium or a virus)'.
findings.truth: A bacterium is the HOST cell, not the vector. The vector is a plasmid or a virus. The sentence was rewritten to the spec's own list (restriction enzymes, sticky ends, ligase, vector such as a bacterial plasmid, host bacteria) and flagged 'Higher tier only' with the code B6.2e.
findings.evidence: bold spec **B6.2e** 'restriction enzymes, sticky ends, ligase, host bacteria and selection using antibiotic resistance markers, vectors e.g. plasmids'

findings.claim: Lesson-to-paper mapping and B4-B6 coverage for a separate-science unit.
findings.truth: THREE of nine lessons carry Paper 1 content: L1 and L2 are B3.3 (known, scope-noted, kept), and L4's DNA structure and protein synthesis are B1.2a-e, also Paper 1. Coverage gaps in the Paper 2 topics are large. B4.1a-d are taught nowhere: material cycling, the role of microorganisms in decomposition, the carbon and water cycles, and the effect of temperature, water content and oxygen on the rate of decomposition (with maths outcome BM4.1i, rate of decay). B5.1d and B5.1e (variants and how they influence phenotype through coding and non-coding DNA), B5.1m (Mendel) and B5.2b (classification and molecular phylogenetics) are absent. B6.1d is absent. Most of B6.3 is absent - B6.3c (HIV/TB, HPV/cervical cancer), B6.3f (a named human infection, TMV, barley powdery mildew, crown gall, and STIs including HIV/AIDS), B6.3g and B6.3h (physical and chemical plant defences), B6.3i, B6.3p (aseptic technique), B6.3q (preclinical and clinical testing), B6.3s (cardiovascular treatments), B6.3v (stem cells), B6.3w and B6.3x. Options: (a) accept the unit as a partial pass and add lessons for B4.1a-d, plant disease and defence, drug development and the medicine statements; (b) move the B1.2 material out of L4 into the Paper 1 unit; (c) leave as is and accept the gap. Recommendation: (a) plus (b) - the missing B6.3 plant-disease and medicine statements are exactly the separate-only depth this unit exists to deliver.
findings.evidence: bold spec B4.1a-d, B5.1d-e, B5.1m, B5.2b, B6.1d, B6.3c, B6.3f-i, B6.3p-x compared against all nine lesson texts

findings.claim: The 'Kidney Failure and Treatments' section runs to five narration blocks, two practice questions, two flashcards, a glossary term and a conclusion takeaway on dialysis and transplants.
findings.truth: None of it has a home in this spec (see F12). Removing it would ripple through narration, the practice set and the glossary, so it was left in place and flagged as background instead. Options: keep as flagged background, or cut the section and replace the two practice questions with B3.3f (osmotic change on cells) and B3.3j items.
findings.evidence: grep of the spec for 'dialysis' returns nothing

findings.claim: Cystic fibrosis, Huntington's disease and pre-implantation genetic diagnosis are taught and carry the 6-mark extended response, but none is named in the spec.
findings.truth: They are legitimate unfamiliar contexts: single-gene inheritance is B5.1i and B5.1j, and PGD is defensible under B6.3w (benefits and risks of gene technology in medicine, practical and ethical considerations). No edit made. All the genetics in this lesson checks out - Bb x Bb gives 3:1 (75/25), Bb x bb gives 1:1, Ff x Ff gives 25 per cent affected and 50 per cent carriers, Hh x hh gives 50 per cent, XX/XY correct.
findings.evidence: bold spec B5.1i, B5.1j, B6.3w; recomputation of all five crosses

findings.claim: Tissue culture is taught as an agricultural solution with its own practice question.
findings.truth: B6.2b lists hydroponics, biological control, gene technology, fertilisers and pesticides - not tissue culture. Cloning appears once in the whole spec, as a practical suggestion (cauliflower) under the B2 cell-division statements. The science is right, so no edit.
findings.evidence: grep of the spec for 'tissue culture' returns nothing; 'cloning' returns one practical suggestion

findings.claim: Several questions ask for two named items but carry one mark: L6 Q2 'Name two types of evidence', L8 Q2 'State two threats', L9 Q2 'State the names of two types of white blood cell'.
findings.truth: A one-mark 'both needed' item is a real board format, so this is defensible rather than wrong. Left alone. Recorded in case the question-type relabel pass wants to lift them to two marks.
findings.evidence: mark-allocation plausibility check

findings.claim: Q4 (write the complementary mRNA sequence for T-A-C-G-G-A) is typed '4 marks - Calculate'.
findings.truth: It is a base-pairing task, not a calculation. The answer A-U-G-C-C-U is correct. Not retyped because 'Calculate' is the established type name for the fourth slot across this unit.
findings.evidence: recomputation: T->A, A->U, C->G, G->C, G->C, A->U

summary: Nine lessons checked against OCR Gateway Biology A. Board structure claims verified: four papers, 1 hour 45 minutes, 90 marks, 50 per cent each; Paper 1/3 = B1-B3 + B7, Paper 2/4 = B4-B6 + B7 with B1-B3 assumed; PAGs 1-8; no SPaG; 6-mark top tariff. 21 FIX findings and 51 edits. The pattern is spec-code drift (14 wrong codes across L1-L4 and one wrong PAG group in L7) plus tier-wrapper faults running both ways: two higher-only wrappers hid both-tier content (L3 biomass efficiency B4.1i-j, L8 genetic modification B6.2d/f/g) while two blocks of genuinely bold content sat unflagged (L2 ADH B3.3i, L4 protein synthesis B1.2d-e). One factual error: a bacterium called a vector when it is the host. Two knowledge checks had two defensible answers (islet/beta cells; template/antisense strand). Every worked number recomputed and correct - percentage change 39.3 and 78.6, biomass efficiency 12.9, Lincoln Index 200/192/180, all five Punnett crosses, the mRNA sequence. No LaTeX leaked into plain-text fields, no banned rubric or board-code strings, no AQA or Edexcel practical wording. Scope notes added to L1 and L2 as briefed. Three ADJUDICATE/NOTE items on out-of-spec content (dialysis, eutrophication exam claim now fixed, tissue culture) and one unit-level ADJUDICATE on paper mapping and large B4.1 and B6.3 coverage gaps.
